title: Markandeya inside the child
hook: a sage swims the flood and finds the whole world inside a child
carry: all unfolds from the one and folds back
tomorrow: a mountain grows to block the sun. what made it bow?

segments.voice: Yesterday, the Sri Yantra's name: Sri is her gift, and pride drives it away. Today, the direction you read it in.
screen: `A WHOLE DIAGRAM IN ONE SHORT WORD.`

segments.voice: The sage Markandeya asks to see the Lord's power, and the vision comes. The world goes under a flood: no shore, no sun, only water and dark wind. He swims alone for what feels like ages. Then, on a banyan branch above the waves, he sees a small child lying on a leaf, glowing, his toe in his mouth. As Markandeya comes close, the child breathes in, and the sage is drawn inside him. There he sees the whole world again: mountains, rivers, cities, even his own hermitage. Then the child breathes out, and he's back in the flood. In the Bhagavata Purana, the child is Vishnu. So: where does everything come from, and where does it go back to?
screen: `A FLOOD, NO SHORE.` → `A CHILD ON A BANYAN LEAF.` → `THE WORLD, BREATHED IN AND OUT.`

segments.voice: Hindu teaching pictures the world in great cycles: it unfolds, and in time it folds back into the one it came from, pralaya, and later unfolds again. Markandeya saw both in a single breath. The Sri Yantra is read the same two ways. Outward from the bindu, where Shiva and Shakti are one: triangles open into triangles, then petals, then rings, out to the square, the world as it's lived. That's srishti, creation. Inward from the square, layer by layer: that's samhara, folding back, the many returning to the one. Not grim; a homecoming. The worship from two days ago walks that road. A neighbor tradition says something close. The Qur'an describes the patient, who say, when misfortune strikes them: "Lo! we are Allah's and lo! unto Him we are returning." What the two share: everything comes from one source and goes back to it, and the going back is a homecoming, not a void. The honest difference: in the Qur'an, God is the Creator, and creation stays distinct from God. In Sri Vidya's reading, the layers unfold from the Goddess as her own expression, and the return is the many folding back into the one.
screen: `PRALAYA: THE WORLD FOLDS BACK.` · `OUTWARD: SRISHTI, CREATION.` · `INWARD: SAMHARA, FOLDING BACK.` · `THE QUR'AN: UNTO HIM WE RETURN.` · `SHARED RETURN; DIFFERENT PICTURE.` · then, large: `ALL UNFOLDS FROM THE ONE, AND FOLDS BACK.`

segments.voice: Close your eyes. On each in-breath, picture the yantra's layers folding gently inward toward the point; on each out-breath, picture them opening back out to the square. Let the breath set the pace, and when the picture fades, just keep the breathing.
The Sri Yantra, read two ways: srishti, unfolding out from the point, and samhara, folding back to it.
Last line for today: all unfolds from the One and folds back. Markandeya saw it in one breath. Day sixteen thirty-seven.
